All right, the recent edits to `src/tui.tsx` were aimed at making the status line stay docked at the bottom of the terminal regardless of how many lines of output appear above it. I introduced `rowsRef` to track the terminal height, used it to compute a dynamic cap for the visible stream, and wrapped the main content in a `<Box flexDirection="column" height={dynRows}>` so that the status line is always rendered at the bottom of that container. I also added a `<Spacer />` before the approval component to push everything down, and ensured the status line markup includes the TPS arrow (`tpsTrend`).

I just built the project with `bunx tsc` and `bun build`, copied the binary to `~/.local/bin/glint`, and launched a fresh tmux session named `glint` with a 110x30 pane. The capture output shows the status line at row 29 (out of 30), confirming that the docking works when the UI first renders with no additional content. The line reads:

```
compound · effort max · ctx 0 · 0 tok · $0.00 · safe · diag on · /help
```

Now I need to verify that the docking remains stable when the UI is actively receiving new output. The status line should stay at the bottom even as the stream grows, and the TPS arrow should update (showing an up or down arrow) as the token‑per‑second metric changes.

The most straightforward way to test this is to feed the running `glint` instance a fairly long prompt that will generate a sizable amount of output over a few seconds. I’ll use `tmux send-keys` to type a request like “write a detailed 400 word essay on terminal emulators, no file, just chat”. After sending the keys and hitting Enter, I’ll give the model a couple of seconds to start streaming its response, then capture the bottom six lines of the pane. This will let me see whether the status line is still at the bottom and whether the TPS arrow has changed from its initial state.

To be thorough, I’ll capture the pane twice: once after a short delay (≈3 seconds) to see the early state, and again after a longer pause (≈4 seconds later) to confirm that the line remains docked throughout the response and that the TPS arrow updates as the throughput changes. The `tmux capture-pane -p | tail -6` command will give me the last six lines, which should include the status line and the prompt line. By echoing a separator between the two captures, I can clearly compare the two snapshots.

Thus, the next action is to run a bash command that sends the prompt, waits, captures the pane, waits a bit more, and captures again. This will provide the evidence I need to confirm that the docking logic works under load and that the TPS indicator behaves as expected.

The appropriate command is:
```bash
tmux send-keys -t glint 'write a detailed 400 word essay on terminal emulators, no file, just chat' && sleep 0.2 && tmux send-keys -t glint Enter && sleep 3 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | tail -6 && echo "===== 4s later =====" && sleep 4 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | tail -6
```
This matches the description “Capture bottom rows twice mid-run to verify docking and tps”. I’ll issue this as a Bash tool call.
